title: Exceptional base change descends from affine opens of its base
statement: Let Λ be a finite commutative ring. Let sq = (g' : X' → X, f' : X' → Y', f : X → Y, g : Y' → Y) be cartesian, with f and f' compactifiable and f' quasi-compact. Suppose that for every affine open immersion j : U → Y, every cartesian restriction sqU = (a : V → X, p : V → U, f, j) with p compactifiable, and every cartesian square sq' = (b : V' → V, p' : V' → U', p, c : U' → U) with p' compactifiable and quasi-compact, the canonical exceptional base-change transformation for sq' is invertible. Then the canonical exceptional base-change transformation for sq is invertible on the whole ordinary unbounded etale derived category.

source.place: Coherences (i) and (iii): restriction of the compactification exchange to a base chart, transposition, and descent.

proof.text: Take the affine cover j_i : U_i → Y. Define V_i = X ×_Y U_i, U'_i = U_i ×_Y Y', and V'_i = X' ×_{Y'} U'_i. Pullback pasting constructs b_i : V'_i → V_i and the square for p_i : V_i → U_i along c_i : U'_i → U_i. Compactifiability and quasi-compactness of p'_i are inherited from f'. For every x in X', choose an affine chart containing g(f'(x)). The range formula for base-changed open immersions gives a point of V'_i over x. Hence the open immersions a'_i : V'_i → X' are jointly surjective.

Evaluate the exceptional base-change transformation at K. For each chart, apply the open-restriction lemma, using the hypothesis for the local square. Thus La'_i* of the component at K is invertible. Exact etale pullback commutes with homology; the jointly surjective open cover detects isomorphisms of every homology sheaf. Hence the component at K, and therefore the natural transformation, is invertible. Lean uses the existing isIso_of_isIso_leftDerivedUpperStar_map_of_jointlySurjective theorem from SmoothDuality.Local for this last deduction.
